Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the run-chase to begin here at Sky Stadium. The two Umpires make their way out to the middle and so do the players of New Zealand who spread out to their respective fielding positions. David Warner and Travis Head are the two openers for Australia. The leading wicket-taker in all men's T20Is, Tim Southee has the new ball in his hands and is all in readiness to bowl the first over of the chase. Let's play...
...The Run Chase...

Right then, Australia must need to get out of the blocks early to chase a mammoth total of 216. They do have an explosive batting order that can take any bowling line-up to the cleaners. New Zealand have enough runs on the board but surely they won't be at ease and would aim to pick quick wickets inside the Powerplay and exert pressure right on. An engaging run-chase is up on the cards. Stay tuned.

Rachin Ravindra is down for a quick chat for his phenomenal batting (68 runs off 35 balls - 2 fours and 6 sixes). Ravindra says that he has watched a lot of cricket growing up here and playing for New Zealand for the first time here is surreal. Adds that he took some time early but Conway going after the bowlers helped him settle down and the partnership gave them a good platform. Praises Allen for his batting and says that he tried to knock it around, and sometimes it works, sometimes it doesn't. Mentions that 200 is a par score here as the wicket is good with short boundaries and the Aussies are a good batting side. He hopes that the Kiwis can defend it. Ends by saying that as a spinner you have to be unpredictable and mix your lengths and see how it goes.

Australia on the other hand, did not start off as intended as Glenn Maxwell was taken to the cleaners in his first over. He was too ordinary with the ball and offered Allen to free his arms and get into the groove. He was followed by Pat Cummins, who was playing his first T20I after the last T20 World Cup. He too, went for too many runs in his first. Mitchell Starc contrastingly bowled a good couple of overs conceding just a run-a-ball and also got rid of the dangerous-looking aggressor Finn Allen which slowed down the scoring rate considerably. They failed to exert the pressure further as every single bowler was being hit out of the park, courtesy of some really ordinary bowling, especially by Zampa and Maxwell. Even the pacers like Cummins and Hazlewood weren't spared in the onslaught. Pat Cummins then broke the most important partnership by dismissing Rachin Ravindra, and he was followed by Mitchell Marsh sending back Devon Conway in the very next over. Mitchell Starc was a busy man in the field as he grabbed two catches as well as picked a crucial wicket. After a decent couple of overs in the slog,  Australia did not finish up cleanly as they conceded 31 runs off the last two overs. And with that, Australia conceded four consecutive 200-plus scores in T20Is.

10 Fours 13 Sixes, and 47 runs off the last five overs. Phew, what an engaging and breathless first half we have had at the Sky Stadium, in Wellington. The hosts elected to bat first and they right on fired on all cylinders as Finn Allen took on the charge. Devon Conway, who was in search of runs, too joined him taking the aggressive route. New Zealand were 50 in no time as Finn Allen struck some brutal boundaries inside the Powerplay before perishing on a quickfire 32 off just 17 rocks. But, he and Conway provided a solid foundation for New Zealand. But the departure of Allen put some brakes on the scoring rate as despite New Zealand being 68/1 after the end of the Powerplay, they struggled to find boundaries with Rachin Ravindra starting off on a sedate note. But, they continued to pinch in singles and doubles and rotated the strike without eating too many deliveries. But once he got into the groove, Rachin Ravindra smoked every poor delivery thrown at him with ease and cleared the fence. He struck 6 sixes and 2 fours in his inning. Devon Conway too, batted aggressively and the two southpaws zoomed up the scoring rate. But the two departed in the span of just two balls scoring 62 and 63 respectively. The two tailored a marvelous 113-run stand and provided a strong platform for the Kiwis to finish on a high. Mark Chapman and Glenn Phillips, were new to the crease without facing a delivery, but they didn't let the pressure creep in. And their valuable contributions in the backend helped them mount 215 runs, making it New Zealand's second-highest score in T20Is.

Only a single to end the innings then! Another slower one, back of a length and around off, Mark Chapman goes through his pull shot early and toe-ends it to the off side for one. 15 runs off the last over. New Zealand finishes on 215/3!

Commentary.Commentary: The skipper, Mitchell Marsh brings himself into the attack now and will bowl the first over after the mandatory Powerplay. He replaces Josh Hazlewood.
Another full delivery, on off, Rachin Ravindra bunts it down to mid on for one more. New Zealand are 68/1 at the end of the Powerplay. This is their highest against Australia in T20Is.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.6: Mitchell Starc to Rachin Ravindra, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Overpitched and around off, Devon Conway drives it through covers for one.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.5: Mitchell Starc to Devon Conway, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Mitchell Starc errs in his line again and pitches this way down the leg side, Devon Conway fails to work it away, Josh Inglis dives to his right but only manages to parry it towards the third man region. It is called a wide and two byes are taken.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.5: Mitchell Starc to Devon Conway, 3 Wides!

Commentary.Commentary: Risky single! This is the slower again, on a length and on ff, Rachin Ravindra pushes it on the up wide of covers and sets off for the run, the fielder has a shy at the bowler's end but misses. It would have been really close if it was direct hit.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.4: Mitchell Starc to Rachin Ravindra, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Back of a length and around off, Rachin Ravindra stabs it towards cover-point.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.3: Mitchell Starc to Rachin Ravindra, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Goes fuller but down the leg side, Rachin Ravindra misses his flick. Wided.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.3: Mitchell Starc to Rachin Ravindra, Wide!

Commentary.Commentary: Rachin Ravindra is in at number 3.

OUT! TAKEN! Mitchell Starc draws first blood! Finn Allen tries the same shot once again but holes out this time. This one is on a good length and around middle, angling in, Finn Allen tries to heave it across the line again, but the ball lobs up off the splice of the bat towards mid-wicket where David Warner takes a dolly. Allen goes after a fiery cameo.
Commentary.Howout: c David Warner b Mitchell Starc
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.2: Mitchell Starc to Finn Allen, OUT! c David Warner b Mitchell Starc.

Commentary.Commentary: In the air...safe! Mitchell Starc rolls his fingers and takes pace off, full and on off, Finn Allen is early into his slog across the line, and gets it from the toe-end of the bat, the ball flies in the air and lands safely over the mid-wicket fielder. Two runs taken.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.1: Mitchell Starc to Finn Allen, 2 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: Mitchell Starc comes back into the attack now.
New Zealand are up and running, firing on all cylinders with Devon Conway finding his nick in time and also Finn Allen who looks aggressive. Will they end up the Powerplay on a high?
Goes full and outside off just near the tramline, Finn Allen gets low and squeezes it towards gully and point but finds the fielder. They do cross for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.6: Josh Hazlewood to Finn Allen, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Tad short in length on the middle and leg channel, Devon Conway is early on the shot and miscues his pull to square leg for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.5: Josh Hazlewood to Devon Conway, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: On the back of a length angling across off, Finn Allen rides on the bounce off the back foot and cuts it to deep point for one.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.4: Josh Hazlewood to Finn Allen, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Classic textbook straight drive! Hazlewood pitches it fuller and on off, Finn Allen presents the full face of the bat before driving it crisply past the left of mid on for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.3: Josh Hazlewood to Finn Allen, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Aims the pads on a tad fuller length, it hits the abdomen area of the southpaw and he runs a leg bye to the leg side.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.2: Josh Hazlewood to Devon Conway, Leg bye.

Commentary.Commentary: Cuts the batter on off on a length, Devon Conway looks to slash it but it passes below his inside edge and then to the keeper.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.1: Josh Hazlewood to Devon Conway, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Change of ends for Josh Hazlewood.
A brave pace-off from Cummins on a length on top of off, Devon Conway waits and cuts it to gully for a single to end the over. Another expensive over. 15 runs from it.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.6: Pat Cummins to Devon Conway, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! The ball is just racing away to the fence. 50 up for the hosts in no time. Cummins intentionally bowls it short and angles into the batter, Devon Conway pulls it from the crease through the gap between deep square leg and mid-wicket for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.5: Pat Cummins to Devon Conway, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! That has been mercilessly struck by Conway! On a nagging length outside off, Devon Conway drags the pull over mid on for a boundary towards long on.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.4: Pat Cummins to Devon Conway, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: On the back of a length angling into the middle and leg channel, Devon Conway tucks it to short mid-wicket off the back foot.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.3: Pat Cummins to Devon Conway, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: SIX! EDGED AND ALL THE WAY INTO THE STANDS! On a hard length around off, Devon Conway swivels hard to pull but takes the leading edge that clears the deep third man fence for a biggie.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.2: Pat Cummins to Devon Conway, Six!

Commentary.Commentary: Around the wicket on a fuller length, which angles in from off, Devon Conway pushes it to mid off getting on his front foot.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.1: Pat Cummins to Devon Conway, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Change from both ends as Pat Cummins comes into the attack now.
Fractionally short in length on off, Devon Conway knocks it to mid off and sneaks a quick single to end the over. Expensive from Maxwell.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.6: Glenn Maxwell to Devon Conway, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Slows the pace and keeps it outside off on a length, Devon Conway swings and misses. Josh Inglis collects it and quickly flashes off the sticks in a blink. The TV  Umpire checks and confirms that Conway's foot is way inside the crease when Inglis disrupts the sticks. Not Out then.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.5: Glenn Maxwell to Devon Conway, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Class from Conway! Drags his length on outside off, Devon Conway rocks back and cuts it through cover-point for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.4: Glenn Maxwell to Devon Conway, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Full, on the stumps, Allen flicks it to mid-wicket for one.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.3: Glenn Maxwell to Finn Allen, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: SIX! Poor and rightly punished! Offers too much of width outside off on a shortish length, Finn Allen flat-bats it over the long off fence for a six.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.2: Glenn Maxwell to Finn Allen, Six!

Commentary.Commentary: SIX! Allen has his intentions pretty clear! Touch short and outside off, Finn Allen waits and thumps it over the sightscreen over the bowler's head for another maximum. Uh oh, Maxwell has overstepped here and it's a No Ball. Free Hit to follow now.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.2: Glenn Maxwell to Finn Allen, No ball and Six!

Commentary.Commentary: Maxi starts from around the wicket on a fuller length around off, Devon Conway covers the off stump and leans ahead before driving it with the spin, and through the covers for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.1: Glenn Maxwell to Devon Conway, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: First bowling change and we will see some spin now as Glenn Maxwell replaces Mitchell Starc.
Sneaks back into the batter from off on a length, Finn Allen charges down the track to whip it over cow corner but misses out on connecting it. End of the over. 13 runs from it.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.6: Josh Hazlewood to Finn Allen, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: On the back of a length angling into the batter on the middle and off-channel, Finn Allen blocks it off the back foot.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.5: Josh Hazlewood to Finn Allen, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! On the charge now Finn Allen! On fuller length offering a lot of width outside off, Finn Allen lofts it over covers with a still head position towards deep extra cover for a boundary on a couple of bounces.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.4: Josh Hazlewood to Finn Allen, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: SIX! Monstrous and the first biggie of the innings! Full and on the stumps, Finn Allen advances a couple of steps ahead and lifts it over the deep mid-wicket for a huge six. What a shot!
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.3: Josh Hazlewood to Finn Allen, Six!

Commentary.Commentary: Finds the gap but a fantastic effort in the deep by Starc. This is on a fullish length just around off, Devon Conway slices it through the cover-point gap. Mitchell Starc sprints from the deep third-man region and slides to his left. Keeps it to two.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.2: Josh Hazlewood to Devon Conway, 3 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: Over the wicket on a fuller length, Devon Conway inside edges to the leg side.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.1: Josh Hazlewood to Devon Conway, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Josh Hazlewood to share the attack.

Oh, that would have been trouble for Allen! Starc guns it on the middle and leg channel with an inward movement, Finn Allen flicks it to short mid-wicket and is already halfway down the track for sneaking a single but Devon Conway sends him back on a sharp call. The fielder there fumbles a bit which saves Allen as he gets back safely to the striker's end. Not a bad over from Starc at all.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.6: Mitchell Starc to Finn Allen, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: This is a vicious short-pitched delivery on the bodyline of Allen, Finn Allen swivels across to pull but misses as the ball further shoots up after pitching. He is getting a good carry.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.5: Mitchell Starc to Finn Allen, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: On a nagging length around off, Devon Conway gets off the mark by dabbing it late to deep third man for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.4: Mitchell Starc to Devon Conway, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: First runs with the bat and Finn Allen is off the mark! On a fullish length around off, Finn Allen whips across the angle to short mid-wicket where Matthew Short misfields and the ball trickles to the deep. They cross for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.3: Mitchell Starc to Finn Allen, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Cannons it on a length on the middle, Finn Allen swings hard but meets only thin air on that one wearing on his body.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.2: Mitchell Starc to Finn Allen, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: WIDE! A bit of inward movement which slides the ball down leg. Wide given.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.2: Mitchell Starc to Finn Allen, Wide!

Commentary.Commentary: Starts off with a peach of a delivery right on! Good seam and good carry! Starc steams in from over the wicket and slants it across off on a hard length, Finn Allen looks to poke but misses.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.1: Mitchell Starc to Finn Allen, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Done with the pre-match formalities! We can see the Australian players spread out and take their fielding positions. Finn Allen and Devon Conway are the two openers for New Zealand. Mitchell Starc has the new ball in hand and is raring to go. Let's play...

We are moments away from the start of the game, but before that, the players from both sides make their way out to the middle and line up for their respective national anthems. It will be Australia's first followed by the national anthem of New Zealand.
Australia (Playing XI) - Travis Head, David Warner, Mitchell Marsh (C), Glenn Maxwell, Josh Inglis (WK), Tim David, Matthew Short, Pat Cummins, Mitchell Starc, Adam Zampa, Josh Hazlewood.

New Zealand (Playing XI) - Finn Allen, Devon Conway (WK), Rachin Ravindra, Glenn Phillips, Mark Chapman, Josh Clarkson (On Debut), Mitchell Santner (C), Adam Milne, Ish Sodhi, Tim Southee, Lockie Ferguson.
Toss Update: New Zealand won the toss and elected to BAT first.

Meanwhile, led by Mitchell Marsh, Australia enters the contest on the back of a triumphant streak against the Windies in both ODIs and T20Is. The team flaunts a formidable batting unit spearheaded by the dynamic openers David Warner and Travis Head. The middle order is fortified by the likes of Mitchell Marsh, Steven Smith, Josh Inglis, Tim David, and the in-form Glenn Maxwell. The seam bowling attack comprises Nathan Ellis, Josh Hazlewood, Mitchell Starc, Pat Cummins, and the very impressive Spencer Johnson, while the spin duo of Adam Zampa and Matthew Short adds depth to the bowling arsenal, with Short also providing aggressive batting prowess when needed. The squad remains largely unchanged from their recent encounter against the Windies and would want to continue their dominance over their neighbors now. Who will take the first match? Will the Kiwis assert their dominance over 'Straya'? Or will the tourists upset the hosts? We shall find out as we bring you the Toss and Team Updates shortly. Stay tuned.

New Zealand, playing on home turf, has enjoyed a stellar home season thus far, triumphing over Bangladesh initially and recently dominating South Africa in a thrilling two-match Test series. Under the leadership of Mitchell Santner, the Kiwis boast a formidable batting lineup characterized by a blend of aggression and finesse. The opening pair of Finn Allen, who has been in a sublime touch lately in the shortest format, and Devon Conway, with the latter aiming to break free from a recent batting slump, will set the tone for the Kiwi innings. Joining the ranks are Will Young and the promising batting sensation Rachin Ravindra. The middle order comprises Glenn Phillips, Mark Chapman, and the skipper Mitchell Santner himself. The bowling department features the pace trio of Lockie Ferguson, Tim Southee, and Adam Milne, supported by Josh Clarkson and Ben Sears, with Ish Sodhi and Santner providing the spin options. While Trent Boult will join the squad in the second and third T20Is.

Hello, and a very warm welcome to our coverage of the First T20I of the 3-match T20I in the Chappell-Hadlee Trophy, as New Zealand are all in readiness to host their big daddy Tasman neighbors Australia, at the Sky Stadium in Wellington. This match ignites the flames of the renowned Trans-Tasman rivalry. The first game will be played in Wellington and the rest two are scheduled to be played in Auckland.
...MATCH DAY...

A new chapter is about to be written in the Trans-Tasmanian rivalry as the men from Down Under have set foot on New Zealand shores for a multi-format series. The two Trans-Tasman rivals, Australia and New Zealand will first lock horns in a three-match T20I series for the Chappell-Hadlee Trophy before the attention turns to the two-match Test series. The T20I series kicks off at the Sky Stadium in Wellington before the caravan shifts to Auckland for the next two games. Both sides will have one eye on the T20 World Cup as they look to fine-tune their preparations for that mega event in the Caribbean and the USA. New Zealand, led by Mitchell Santner, enter the series with confidence after a convincing 4-1 victory over Pakistan. In the batting department, the onus will fall on Devon Conway to hold the innings, with the likes of Finn Allen and Will Young expected to perform the aggressor role. As for Rachin Ravindra, he will be keen to stake a claim for a spot in the T20 World Cup squad. Mark Chapman and Glenn Phillips will be relied upon for quick runs, with the latter more than handy with his off-breaks. Ish Sodhi and skipper Mitchell Santner will shoulder much of the burden in the spin department for the hosts. New Zealand's squad announcement was headlined with the return of Trent Boult to the T20I setup after 15 months. However, he will be available only for the last two T20Is. Tim Southee, Adam Milne, and Lockie Ferguson are the pace bowling options Santner will have at his disposal in the series opener. On the other hand, Australia arrive at near full strength, fresh from a series win over the West Indies. Mitchell Marsh will continue to lead the side and will play a key role, more importantly with the bat. Other than him, David Warner and Travis Head are the other usual suspects at the top of the order. There will be no shortage of firepower in the middle order with the presence of Glenn Maxwell, Josh Inglis, Tim David, and Matthew Wade. Pat Cummins, Josh Hazlewood, and Mitchell Starc form the crux of the pace department. Nathan Ellis and Spencer Johnson are the other seam options, whereas leggie Adam Zampa will spearhead the spin attack. As the Trans-Tasman rivals renew their age-old rivalry, the stage is set for a cracker of a series. Who will land the first punch? We shall find out.
